newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian refinery shut briefly due to water shortage.
newsitem.headline: Indian refinery shut briefly due to water shortage.

text.p: Indian state-owned refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd plans to keep its 150,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery on the southwest coast of India shut for one or two days, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The shutdown is only for a short time...it will be solved in a day or two," he said.
The spokesman said the restart would depend on when Kerala Water Authority was able to resume water supplies.
Officials of the water supply department could not be reached immediately for comment.
The Cochin spokesman said one of the water authority's dams had been shut down and this had reduced water supply to the refinery and forced it to close on Monday.
"It is very transient, a very temporary phenomenon," he said.
But the refinery had products in stock to provide one week's supply and sufficient ullage to take crude deliveries, he said.
"This is the first time the refinery has had to shut due to this reason," he said.
He said the refinery planned to avoid this problem in future as it had just applied to the state government for permission to build its own pipeline from a nearby river to source its own water.
